findings.message: The main meaning 'this five-syllable (hymn)' / 'यह पञ्चाक्षर (स्तोत्र)' reads the word as the hymn, but none of the evidence says that. The only explicit translation, sanskritdocuments-panch.md, has 'this sacred five-syllabled mantra, (namaH shivAya)'. gitapress-stotraratnavali.md has 'इस पवित्र पञ्चाक्षरका पाठ', which could mean either one. In mw-pancakshara.md, pañcākṣara is only an adjective, 'consisting of 5 syllables'; that fits the five-syllable prayer, while the hymn is only named after it. The prayer reading is recorded under alternatives, so this is not a fail. But the less-supported reading is the main one and confidence is 'high'. A human should decide which reading comes first.
findings.suggested_fix: Either make the prayer reading the main one (en 'this five-syllable prayer (namaḥ śivāya)', hi 'यह पञ्चाक्षर मन्त्र (नमः शिवाय)') and keep 'hymn' as the alternative, or keep 'hymn' first and lower confidence to 'medium'.
